title: Vibe Coding
lede: Building software you can't write by hand. A few questions on scoping an idea, steering the tool and telling a working prototype from a convincing one.
description: Building software you can't write by hand. Test how you scope an idea, steer the tool and tell a working prototype from a convincing one.

questions.q: The term 'vibe coding' has become widely used to describe a new way of building software with AI. Who is credited with coining the term?
questions.why: Andrej Karpathy popularised the term to describe building software by describing intent and iterating with an AI, rather than writing every line by hand.

questions.q: You have an idea for an internal business application and want to use Claude Code to turn it into a working prototype. Which workflow is most effective?
questions.why: Exploring the problem and planning before generating code keeps the AI aligned with what you actually want, instead of producing code first and figuring out the plan after.

questions.q: You ask Claude Code to build a simple internal dashboard. You want the AI to understand what the application should achieve, what information it will use, what it should produce, and how it should be structured visually. Which set of information provides the strongest foundation for the prompt?
questions.why: Goals, inputs, outputs, and layout cover the essentials of what the app needs to do and look like — everything else can be figured out or adjusted later.

questions.q: Your team is considering using vibe coding for several initiatives. Which project is generally the best fit for vibe coding today?
questions.why: Vibe coding is strongest for fast prototyping and validating ideas. Complex, regulated, or mission-critical systems need the rigor of traditional engineering practice.

questions.q: You are working on a large project with Claude Code. Your team has specific coding conventions, architecture decisions, and instructions about how the AI should modify the codebase. What is the primary purpose of a CLAUDE.md or similar instructions file?
options: To store your API keys and passwords securely
To provide context and guidelines to the AI about your project, coding preferences, and conventions
To automatically deploy your code to production
To track version history of your files
questions.why: A persistent instructions file saves you from re-explaining conventions in every new session and keeps output consistent as the project grows.

questions.q: Your finance team wants a vibe-coded tool that automatically calculates and files statutory tax payments for the company. Why is this a poor fit for vibe coding today?
options: Vibe coding tools can't generate any financial calculations
It touches compliance and real money with no room for silent errors — exactly the profile vibe coding is weakest on
Tax rules never change, so there's nothing to prototype
It would take too many prompts to describe
questions.why: Vibe coding shines for MVPs and internal tools where a bug is inconvenient. Regulated, high-stakes work — money, compliance, safety — needs the rigor, testing and accountability of a proper engineering process, not a fast prototype.

questions.q: You've been vibe coding an internal tool for a few hours and just asked for a big change that broke something that used to work. What habit would have saved you the most time?
options: Avoiding version control since it slows down fast iteration
Committing or saving a working checkpoint before each significant change, so you can roll back
Only ever making one change per day
Rewriting the entire app from scratch every time something breaks
questions.why: Frequent checkpoints — a commit, a saved copy, a version snapshot — turn 'something broke and I don't know what' into a quick rollback instead of a rebuild. This matters more with AI-generated code, since changes can be large and hard to review line by line.
